item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 39110140984.

The short draft that the pipeline sent back twice

The first script draft came in at 2694 words against a target of 3400. The pipeline did not ship it. It sent the draft back for expansion, up to two passes, and what shipped was 3423 words. That is 23 words over target, so the expand passes did their job, but the gap is the story: the generator's first attempt ran about 21 percent short and needed the retry loop to reach length.

The voice split held at 0.87, Casey over Riley, and the AI-tell pattern check recorded zero hits. Neither of those numbers was at risk on this run.

Two takes came back short from TTS

Two text-to-speech takes returned shorter than their word counts predicted. Each was retried once. One retry still came back short. For that segment the pipeline kept the longer of the two takes, so no content was dropped from the episode. The audio ran 22.3 minutes at 20.5 MB.

The short-take count is two and the still-short retry count is one. The second number does not mean one segment is missing from the audio. It means one segment is the one where the retry did not produce a full-length take, and the longer take was used in its place. Whether that take is complete is not something the run measured.

The roundup cut 68 stories and the citations did not fully hold

The roundup pool was larger than one segment could air. The airtime budget, set by NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT, cut 68 stories. The pipeline treats that as expected: the pool is deliberately oversized, and a cut story can air on a day where it fits better.

The cuts left a visible tension in the citations. Of 18 roundup citations, 14 matched the aired content. Of four deep-dive citations, three matched. So four citations did not align: one in the roundup and one in the deep dive. The facts do not say which citations failed or why, and this review does not guess.

What the deep dives covered

The four deep dives were drawn from the Gulf attacks coverage in the NYT Business feed, a WIRED piece on microplastics reacting with water, a TechCrunch story on Mosqitter's AI-powered mosquito traps, and an NYT Top Stories piece on worlds more habitable than Earth. The episode's debate question asks whether long-term environmental and scientific monitoring should be trusted and acted on before its implications are confirmed, and how such records should be funded, governed, and sustained. The four deep dives are a loose fit for that question, which is a matter of editorial choice, not a pipeline failure.

Runs and spend

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific, zero minutes late, and finished at 1:53 AM Pacific with a success conclusion. Fallback 1 started at 2:05 AM Pacific and finished at 2:06 AM Pacific, also a success. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run producing this review and has no finish time yet. Its conclusion is null. The fallback runs were scheduled as backups, and their successful completion does not by itself show that the primary's output was replaced.

The slowest step was Deploy to GitHub Pages at 1092 seconds, followed by Checkout repository at 776 seconds and Generate episode script at 491 seconds. Script generation alone consumed 57,310 Anthropic input tokens. The service call counts were brave-search 8, kagi-extract 4, claude 10, and brave-answers 4. The video is 79.3 MB at 22.3 minutes, and the RSS feed now lists 263 episodes.

The primary run needed the full pipeline. The script step took 619 seconds and rendering the audio took 312 seconds. Deploying to GitHub Pages took 326 seconds, longer than the publish step at 109 seconds. The deploy was the second-slowest step after the script.

item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38871365504.

The script came in short and was padded, not the other way round

The first draft of the script ran 3,129 words against a target of 3,400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes. What shipped was 3,412 words, which clears the target by 12. The padding was done by the same machinery that wrote the first draft, so the number that reached the listener is not evidence that the first draft was complete.

Two things in the quality block are worth reading against that. The AI-tell pattern check found 0 hits in the shipped script. The voice ratio of Casey to Riley came in at 0.84. Neither number says anything about whether the expand passes added substance or only length.

Six stories aired out of order after two repair passes failed to fix it

The roundup order degraded. Six stories still aired after a later block, even after 2 repair passes. The pipeline did not drop them or re-cut the segment. It let them run in the wrong place and logged the degradation. A listener hears a story from the wrong part of the day's sequence, and nothing in the audio signals that.

The same segment is where the citation numbers are weakest for the deep dives. Roundup citations matched 16 of 17. Deep dive citations matched 1 of 4. The roundup count is a strong match. The deep-dive count means three of the four deep dives have a citation the pipeline could not align to its source, which is a larger gap than anything the roundup shows.

The roundup pool is much bigger than the airtime

The pipeline dropped 59 stories from the roundup pool to fit the airtime budget set by NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT. That is the design: the pool is meant to exceed what one segment can carry, and a cut story can come back on a day where it fits better. The 59 are not failures. They are the cost of a fixed airtime, and the pipeline will not show which of them a listener would have wanted.

The four deep dives drew on different sources: Global News, Fast Company, Wildfire Today and NYT Business. They covered a parole decision in British Columbia, heat exposure, Los Angeles fire danger, and California's Proposition 45. The debate question the episode was built around asks who bears the cost of protecting people from wildfire and extreme heat, and whether faster housing review and public ownership of warnings and wildlife data make communities safer or mostly favor developers. Only one of the four deep-dive citations matched, so the sourcing behind that question is the thinnest part of the episode.

Three runs, all on time, one still running

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:30 AM Pacific. It completed with success and was 0 minutes late. Fallback 1 started and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific, also successful, also 0 minutes late. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run writing this review and has not finished. The fallbacks did not fire because the primary failed. They were scheduled, and the primary succeeded.

The slowest step was script generation at 534 seconds, followed by GitHub Pages deployment at 350 seconds and audio rendering at 266 seconds. Checkout took 75 seconds, publishing 90 seconds, and the video render and YouTube upload 132 seconds. Every step concluded successfully.

The output is 20.7 minutes of audio and 71.7 MB of video

The audio runs 20.7 minutes and is 18.9 MB. The video is 71.7 MB and also runs 20.7 minutes. The RSS feed now lists 261 episodes. The script consumed 62,718 Anthropic input tokens across 11 Claude calls. The service breakdown shows 12 Brave search calls and 4 Brave answers calls. The input-token figure is a count of tokens and says nothing about cost.

The 3,412-word script at 20.7 minutes is the number to hold against the 3,400-word target and the 3,129-word first draft. The audio length is what the listener gets. The gap between the first draft and the shipped script is what the pipeline had to do to reach it.

item.title: [Cariboo Signals Reviews] Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 14, 2026
item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38532679445.

The show was short and the pipeline padded it

The first script draft came in at 2230 words against a target of 3400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes. What shipped was 3237 words, which is 163 words under target, not on it. The draft ran 1170 words short of target, so the expand passes recovered most of the gap but not all of it.

The expand passes did not add new reporting. The body backfill that would have filled thin articles ran out of budget: Brave body-backfill calls were spent at 12. The remaining thin articles kept their stub bodies, and the pipeline flagged them as possibly cut for sparseness. So the listener got a longer script built partly from articles that had little to say, and some of those may have been dropped anyway.

Fifty-three roundup stories were cut, and that was the design

The roundup pool was larger than one segment could air. The airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT) cut 53 stories. Those stories remain in the pool and can resurface on a day that matches them better. Nothing about the cut is a failure. It is the cost of a fixed airtime budget against a larger pool.

The count sits next to the sparse-body problem. The pipeline had room to air 53 fewer stories than it curated, yet it still had to expand a short draft and still kept thin articles it could not fill. The curated count and the aired count disagree in the direction of more material than airtime, while the script disagrees in the direction of less material than target. Both are true on the same run.

Citations held on the roundup and slipped on the deep dives

All 15 roundup citations matched their sources. On the deep dives, 1 of 3 citations matched. The three deep-dive stories were Hackster items on a package-measuring system, lakebed mapping, and protecting a Raspberry Pi 5 from sudden power loss. The two unmatched citations were the weakest link in an otherwise clean run, and the facts do not say why they failed to match.

The voice split and the AI-tell check

The Casey-to-Riley voice ratio came in at 0.88, and the AI-tell pattern check recorded 0 hits. The check is clean, but a 0.88 ratio means the two hosts sat close to each other in how much they spoke, not that the dialogue was balanced in any stronger sense.

Audio held, short TTS takes were retried

The audio runs 18.8 minutes at 17.2 MB. The video runs 18.8 minutes at 65.2 MB. Two TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicted. Each was retried once, and both retries were still short. The pipeline kept the longer take in each case, so no text was dropped from the episode. The short takes are a fact about the audio's pacing; the facts do not say whether they affected how the lines sounded.

Three runs, all green, one still running

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:32 AM Pacific, with no minutes late. Fallback 1 started and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run producing this review and has no finish time yet. Two of the three runs completed, and the first two both succeeded. The generate-script step took 610 seconds, the longest in the run, and the deploy step took 366 seconds. The episode count stands at 259.

Spend, by service

The run used 62,399 Anthropic input tokens. Brave search was called 28 times, Claude 17 times, and Brave answers 4 times. Those numbers measure calls and tokens, not cost, and the facts give no dollar figure. The 12 Brave body-backfill calls that exhausted their budget are part of the 28 search calls.

item.title: [Cariboo Signals Reviews] Episode Review — Cariboo Signals, October 13, 2026
item.dc:creator: Cariboo Signals Reviews
item.description:
What the pipeline did, what broke, and what it chose when something broke. Run 38366919269.

Four short TTS takes, one kept at full length

The most consequential thing in this run is not a failure but a fallback. Four TTS takes came back shorter than their word count predicts. Each was retried once. Of those retries, four were still short. The pipeline kept the longer of the two takes for each, so nothing is dropped from the episode.

The tradeoff is that a short take is evidence the audio may not match the script. Keeping the longer take preserves the content but does not verify that every word was spoken. The facts do not say whether the four still-short segments are truncated, only that the longer take was kept.

The script came in under target and was expanded

The first draft ran 2,923 words against a target of 3,400. The pipeline sent it back for up to two expand passes. The shipped script is 2,935 words, which is 465 words short of the 3,400 target. The expand passes added 12 words over the first draft. The episode ran 17.6 minutes of audio at 16.1 MB.

The gap between the target and the shipped length is the number to watch. The expand passes recovered almost none of the shortfall, so the length target is not being met by this mechanism.

Citations: 11 of 15 roundup, 2 of 3 deep dive

Eleven of 15 roundup citations matched. Two of 3 deep-dive citations matched. The unmatched citations are the ones a listener or maintainer would need to check by hand. The three deep dives were Small Farm Canada on light and nutrient use, Quartz on grocery staples and El Niño, and Country Life on sheep farming and architecture.

The roundup pool was far larger than the airtime. Of the stories curated, 47 were dropped by the airtime budget (NEWS_ROUNDUP_COUNT). That is by design. A dropped story can resurface on a day when it fits better. But it means the 15 roundup citations are a small slice of what the pipeline read, and the citation ratio describes only the aired slice.

Ratio of voices and the AI-tell check

The voice ratio of Casey over Riley is 0.85, so the two hosts are close to balanced in speaking share. The AI-tell pattern check recorded zero hits.

Runs and spend

The primary run started at 1:05 AM Pacific and finished at 1:27 AM Pacific with a success conclusion. Fallback 1 started and finished at 2:05 AM Pacific, also a success. Fallback 2, at 3:05 AM Pacific, is the run producing this review and has not finished. Both completed runs were zero minutes late.

The Anthropic input was 58,919 tokens. API calls were 8 to brave-search, 10 to claude, and 4 to brave-answers. The slowest step was script generation at 456 seconds, followed by GitHub Pages deploy at 341 seconds and audio rendering at 248 seconds.
